subject: Attestation request: 24h hotpatch SLA for critical CVE affecting kernel packages
messages:
From: Elena Cruz <security@blinkpay.com>
To: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: hotpatch SLA attestation + scan evidence

Hi Markus,

Quick ask from our security team: BlinkPay just flagged a high-severity kernel CVE in one of the base images we run. For contract/inventory reasons we need a written attestation that Redwood will commit to a 24-hour remediation SLA for critical (CVSS 9-10) CVEs that affect our deployed environments, and the supporting evidence showing scan cadence and recent results.

Specifically can you provide: 
- A short attestation letter we can include in our SOC2 folder confirming the 24h hotpatch SLA for critical CVEs on Dedicated/Private deployments;
- Scan cadence (how often infra images & hosts are scanned) and the last 30 days of scan results summary;
- The escalation path and confirmation of patch windows / pre-approved emergency windows and rollback policy;
- Any artifacts you can share (scan logs, runbook excerpts, or a signed PDF).

We need this for an internal audit and may include it in our third-party SIG request. If you can get something over by EOD PT today that would be ideal — BlinkPay is asking for an expedited assurance.

Thanks,
Elena Cruz
Security Engineer 
BlinkPay
[security@blinkpay.com]

--
Attachment: none in initial request
From: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Cruz <security@blinkpay.com>
Cc: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>, laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: hotpatch SLA attestation + scan evidence

Elena —

Thanks for the heads up and the clear ask. We can commit to the requested attestation for BlinkPay's Dedicated and Private deployments: Redwood will remediate critical (CVSS 9-10) vulnerabilities affecting customer workloads within 24 hours of a validated exploitability assessment or proof-of-concept that affects the deployed surface. That commitment is scoped to vulnerabilities in third-party components (OS kernel, runtime libs) and to Redwood-managed components in Dedicated/Private.

What I am sending now: 
- Attached: redwood-vm-sla-24h.pdf — a short attestation letter suitable for SOC2/SIG submission (PDF).
- Attached: scan-log-20260820.csv — sanitized scan extract for the last 30 days (host IDs redacted) and a 30-day cadence summary.
- Summary below of the escalation & patch window process.

Escalation & patching (summary):
- Detection: automated weekly host/image scans + continuous monitoring for published CVEs.
- Triage: vulnerabilities triaged by severity within 2 hours of detection; criticals (CVSS 9-10) receive immediate ownership.
- Remediation SLA: patch build/validation and staged rollout completed within 24 hours of validation. Emergency hotpatching is available outside normal windows.
- Rollback: all hotpatch rollouts include a validated rollback / snapshot plan; we maintain snapshots for Dedicated customers for a minimum of 72 hours post-deploy.
- Contact path: 
  * First escalation: Security Ops (kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com)
  * Next: Customer Reliability (laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com)
  * Exec escalation: markus_klein@redwoodinference.com

I attached the artifacts above and uploaded a drive folder with full evidence (redacted as needed): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Aq-example-VM-Evidence

We will prepare a signed attestation (DocuSign or signed PDF) — Kim and Laura, can you confirm availability to sign and push the signed copy back to Elena by EOD PT?

Markus Klein
Director, Security & Trust
Redwood Inference

Markus —

Appreciate the quick turnaround and the attachments. Two quick follow-ups: 
1) For contract review we need an executed (signed) attestation PDF or a DocuSign link that we can store in our SIG evidence folder. DocuSign is preferred.
2) Can you briefly clarify whether the 24h SLA includes 0-day exploitation windows discovered externally (e.g., public PoC) or if it requires a validated exploitability assessment from your internal triage team first? BlinkPay wants clarity to avoid ambiguity during audits.

If you can include a short line specifying scope (POC vs internal verification) in the signed letter that will close the loop.

Thanks again — we can escalate internally on our side to give you the runway if needed.

—Elena

From: markus_klein <markus_klein@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Fwd: Re: Request: hotpatch SLA attestation + scan evidence

Elena —

Attaching the signed attestation. We added the requested scope language: the 24-hour remediation SLA is triggered by either (a) publication of a public proof-of-concept/active exploit affecting a component in your deployed stack, or (b) an internal validated exploitability assessment that concludes the vulnerability is exploitable in your environment. In short: public PoC triggers SLA; internal validation can also trigger when necessary.

See attached signed-attestation-20260821.pdf. I also included a short appendix in the PDF describing rollback policy and the snapshot retention window.

If you want DocuSign instead, Kim — can you spawn a DocuSign envelope and route to Elena? Otherwise this signed PDF should be fine for BlinkPay's SIG.

Best,
Markus
